Risk officer read: I'd refuse any size, or at most a minimal $5 ticket if the desk insists, with a 20% stop and 15-minute hold.

Reasons: the 30-minute return is +132% and the last 15 minutes show 339% return on $90k volume. That is a parabolic run, and the 4.4% drawdown from the high is too small to confirm a base. Sell volume is almost equal to buy volume (sell/buy 1.009) with 764 sellers in the last 15 minutes, so supply is being distributed heavily. Launch bot present and bundle share of 33% point to engineered early flow. Pool depth of 127.7 SOL is thin for a $20 round trip cost of 1.4-5.1%, and a 30-second latency on a fast-moving coin means our fill could be well off the decision price.

Against that: it's alive, organic-classed, with no airdrop dump and low top-3 concentration. Still, the base rate for chasing post-graduation parabolic moves is poor. Skip unless there is a clear reason the desk can articulate.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is thin, but there are a few real points in the brief.

Demand looks broad and recent: 879 buyers and 764 sellers in the last 15 minutes, $90.7k volume, and a +33.9% return over that window. Post-graduation, buyers outnumber the agent's buys in the first two minutes (207 buyers, 77 SOL), and the top-5 buyer share is 23%, so no single wallet dominates early flow. Concentration is low (top-3 holders at 4.7%), there is no airdrop dump, and the drawdown from the 30-minute high is only 4.4%. Net flow of +25.7 SOL over 15 minutes shows buying slightly outweighing selling.

The case against is stronger. The sell-to-buy ratio of 1.009 in the launch window means sellers matched buyers almost exactly, and the bundle share of 33% suggests a meaningful slice of early activity was coordinated. A launch bot was present. The coin is 30 minutes old, past the window where most organic memecoins fade, and the 30-minute return of +132% means much of the move is already priced in. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% are significant against a 4.4% drawdown.

My read: there is a real demand signal, but it is not clean enough to outweigh the base rates for buying a coin this late in i

The coin is up 132% over 30 minutes, so exit liquidity is being sold into. In the last 15 minutes, 366 SOL was sold against 392 SOL bought, with net flow of only +25.7 SOL and 764 sellers, so the buying is thinning while holders take profit. The first two minutes post-graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.009, meaning sellers matched buyers almost exactly, and a launch bot was present. Price is already 4.4% off its high, and with a 127 SOL pool, a $20 ticket faces 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs. A small pullback would be fully consumed by fees, and insider distribution could push the curve much lower before the next hour.
